blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, classifying an item as taxable or not is often less obvious than the textbook suggests. A training course paid for by the company — is it a taxable benefit or a legitimate business expense? A small gift to a client — deductible or non-deductible? A reimbursed meal during a long trip — neutral or a disguised benefit?

Each of these has an answer in the local rules, but the answer often depends on small details. A training course that genuinely supports the employee's role is usually not taxable. A gift above a certain value often is. A meal during a documented business trip is different from a meal during a leisure evening.

A good intermediate tax professional does not guess. They document the reasoning for every borderline case the first time it appears, and then follow the same reasoning consistently afterwards — so that the tax office, if it asks, gets the same clear answer every time.

items.q: According to the text, why is classifying an item harder than the textbook suggests?
options: The local rules do not exist yet
The answer often depends on small details
Textbooks are usually out of date
items.why: "the answer often depends on small details" — o texto é claro sobre isso.

items.q: When is a training course usually NOT taxable, according to the text?
options: When it genuinely supports the employee's role
When it is paid in instalments
When it happens outside working hours
items.why: "A training course that genuinely supports the employee's role is usually not taxable."

items.q: What does a good intermediate tax professional do with borderline cases?
options: Treats every item as taxable to be safe
Documents the reasoning the first time and follows it consistently
Waits for the tax office to decide
items.why: "They document the reasoning for every borderline case the first time it appears, and then follow the same reasoning consistently."

items.q: The contrast between a meal on a documented business trip and a meal during a leisure evening suggests that…
options: leisure meals are always taxable benefits
trips should be avoided to reduce tax
the context of an expense, not just its type, decides how it is treated
items.why: Inferência: o mesmo item (refeição) muda de classificação conforme o contexto documentado.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The same detail can change whether an item is taxable
Consistency helps when the tax office asks questions
Documenting reasoning early saves trouble later
Since the rules are complex, a quick guess is good enough for borderline items
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende o oposto — "does not guess" e documenta o raciocínio.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando o memorando interno. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, I'm putting together a short internal memo, because we keep having the same argument every month about three items, and I want us to decide the logic once.

Take training first. Last month someone asked me whether the leadership course counted as a taxable benefit. I told them that if the course genuinely supports the person's role, we treat it as a business expense — not taxable. So I'll write that down as our rule, with one line of reasoning next to it.

Gifts are trickier. A small branded notebook to a client is fine, but anything above the local threshold I'd flag as non-deductible. The value is what tips it over, so the memo will state the exact figure rather than leave people guessing.

And meals. A reimbursed dinner during a documented trip is neutral. A dinner on a leisure evening that quietly ends up on expenses is a disguised benefit, and we should not be paying for it. The difference is the paperwork behind it.

The point of all this is consistency. If the tax office ever asks, I want every one of us giving the same answer, because we wrote the reasoning down the first time — not because we happened to remember it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Charlotte writing the internal memo?
options: She is training a new hire
The team keeps having the same argument every month about three items
A new law changed the rules
items.why: "we keep having the same argument every month about three items, and I want us to decide the logic once."

items.q: How does Charlotte say the leadership training course should be treated?
options: As a business expense, if it genuinely supports the person's role
items.why: "if the course genuinely supports the person's role, we treat it as a business expense — not taxable."

items.q: What decides whether a gift becomes non-deductible, according to Charlotte?
options: Whether it is given in person
Its value, once it goes above the local threshold
items.why: "anything above the local threshold I'd flag as non-deductible. The value is what tips it over."

items.q: When Charlotte says "The difference is the paperwork behind it," she means that…
options: the trip must be approved in advance
documentation is what separates a neutral meal from a disguised benefit
items.why: Inferência: é a documentação da viagem que distingue uma refeição neutra de um benefício disfarçado.

items.q: What does Charlotte most want the memo to achieve?
options: Faster answers, even if they vary
Everyone giving the same answer because the reasoning was written down
items.why: Inferência: ela enfatiza consistência — "the same answer… because we wrote the reasoning down the first time."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A gift above the limit is treated as non-deductible." Something deductible is…
options: an amount that can be subtracted from taxable profit
a payment made in cash only
an expense that must be repaid twice
a bonus paid to the client
items.why: Deductible = dedutível: pode ser abatido do lucro tributável. Non-deductible é o oposto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The company agreed to ___ the employee for the meals he paid for during the trip."
items.why: To reimburse = reembolsar: devolver ao empregado o que ele gastou.

items.q: "A dinner on a leisure night that ends up on expenses is a disguised benefit." This means…
options: a personal perk presented as if it were a business cost
a gift given to a client
a benefit that is legally tax-free
a benefit that everyone can see clearly
items.why: Disguised benefit = benefício disfarçado: uma vantagem pessoal mascarada de despesa de negócio.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A training course, a small gift, a reimbursed meal — each one is a ___ that could go either way."
items.why: Borderline case = caso limítrofe: pode ser classificado de duas formas conforme os detalhes.

items.q: "We apply the same rule consistently every month." This means we apply it…
options: in the same way each time, without varying
only when the tax office asks
items.why: Consistently = consistentemente: da mesma maneira, sempre — o oposto de decidir caso a caso ao acaso.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de contabilidade e tributação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the classification before we file it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new classification memo to every regional office next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two accountants pushed back on treating the meal as neutral." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to document each case but never followed through." They…
options: delegated it to the tax office
failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Before the audit, let's tighten up how we record borderline expenses." To tighten up means to…
options: make it stricter and more careful
items.why: Tighten up = apertar, tornar mais rigoroso e cuidadoso um processo ou controle.
